note: Big advertising boards on gables, roofs and one embankment (claude/billboards, rule billboards). Each board says what Street View shows (2024 imagery, looked at, never kept or traced) in our own words, or that it is PLACED: a blind gable / flat roof facing a main road where such boards hang in Brussels, with no board there today. Posters are INVENTED (no real brand, logo or ad art). `u`: the board's centre along its face from the face's left end SEEN FROM OUTSIDE (m); `y0`: the poster's foot over the face's base line (m). `at` is written by tools/billboards/billboards.mjs --write from the city's own faces / roofs / ground and checked by the gate row `billboards`.

dropped.why: review 2026-11-24: an 8 x 3 m panel on the north gable of UrbIS 604726 (J5) was hidden from Ch. de Waterloo by the J4 building 8.6 m in front of it (the old check read only its own tile); no height on that gable clears it from the street (the gable top is 14.2 m)

review 2026-11-24: the 6 x 8 m canvas on UrbIS 531023 (Av. Brugmann) cannot be seen whole from any street eye 15-60 m in front: the buildings before it hide its lower part, wherever it hangs on that face

boards.place: Place Emile Danco (Le Globe), the pink gable over the shops
boards.source: Street View Apr 2024 (look only): a framed board about 4 x 3 m on the tall blind pink gable at the corner of Place Danco, about 7 m up, over the one-storey shops, facing the square (east-north-east). Placed on the part of that gable the city's data shows exposed.

boards.place: Ch. de Saint-Job by the Saint-Job railway viaduct (Rue Engeland / Rue du Chateau d'Or junction)
boards.source: Street View Jun 2024 (look only): a free-standing board about 4 x 3 m on two legs at the foot of the rail embankment north of Ch. de Saint-Job, just east of the viaduct's arches, facing the junction (east-south-east): the board by the Engeland bridge, 250 m from Ch. d'Alsemberg.

boards.place: Ch. de Saint-Job just west of the Saint-Job viaduct, facing the traffic from Ch. d'Alsemberg
boards.source: PLACED (owner 2026-11-24: a rotating prism board near the Engeland / Ch. d'Alsemberg bridge): a free-standing trivision on two legs on the open ground just west of the viaduct's arches, facing west-north-west down Ch. de Saint-Job towards Ch. d'Alsemberg (250 m); Street View shows no prism board here today (the real board stands east of the arches: stjob_viaduct). The blind gable 6 m west (UrbIS 520785) was tried first: the roof kit's chimney stack runs down it where the board would hang.

boards.place: Ch. de Waterloo at Langeveld (No. 826), the blind gable seen by the traffic going up the chaussée
boards.source: PLACED: the 14 m blind party wall standing over its neighbour at Ch. de Waterloo 826 (Street View Apr 2019, look only: only a shop's own small signs lower on these walls), raised to 11.5 m so that it clears the roofs in front, seen from the chaussee 35 m away; a 4.5 x 2 m trivision (prism) board; no prism board there today. (UrbIS 520249 next door was tried first: the roof kit's chimney stack runs down it.)

boards.place: Place de Saint-Job, the flat roof behind the square
boards.source: PLACED: a roof board on legs on the 10 m flat roof by Ch. de Saint-Job, facing the road and the square (south-south-east); no board there today.
